people.name: Rob Jetten
people.role: Prime Minister of the Netherlands and Minister of General Affairs since 23 February 2026, leading a minority cabinet of D66, VVD and CDA; D66 party leader since August 2023

D66.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
D66.position: D66 leads the cabinet that continues the national strategy and raised the security fund. In the April 2026 debate MP Bamenga asked for action against AI-generated Holocaust imagery, more support for enforcing house rules at universities, continuous evaluation of the strategy and attention for present-day Jewish life in education. He said the security fund originated in a motion by Rob Jetten.

D66.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
D66.position: Governs with VVD and CDA under a coalition agreement promising 'more control and reduced inflow' together with decent reception. Its election programme supports the EU Pact, keeps the Spreidingswet, and wants a statutory children's pardon and work and language lessons from day one. In the House D66 voted against repealing the Spreidingswet (23 June 2026). In the Senate the D66 group reached a 'negative judgement' on the Schoof-cabinet bills, mainly over criminalising illegal stay, and Senator Dittrich voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet; the group voted for the Pact implementation act.

D66.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
D66.position: Supports taxing actual returns and voted for both the February 2026 bill and the November amending bill. NOS reports D66 leans towards a yearly growth tax and opposed funding a capital gains tax at the expense of lower incomes; MP Oosterhuis called the minister's funding a fairly creative reading of the budget rules. D66 made the Tax Plan deal with CDA, PRO and Volt that adds a 38.5% top rate.

D66.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
D66.position: D66 campaigned on building ten new cities and on phasing out the mortgage interest deduction over at least 15 years. In December 2025 D66 and CDA jointly proposed a gradual phase-out once compensation through income tax is possible. In the coalition agreement D66 accepted that the tax treatment of the home stays unchanged; on 12 May 2026 it nevertheless voted for a motion to reverse the automatic increase in the deduction rate.

D66.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
D66.position: D66 wants less low-paid labour migration and more targeted migration of skilled and knowledge workers, with strict conditions for employers and the Roemer recommendations as a basis. As a coalition party it supports the coalition agreement. In 2026 it voted for the guiding band for labour migration and the meat-sector agency ban, against work permits for EU workers and against the SGP motion to consider non-EU labour migration only as a last resort; it voted against 20-year naturalisation and for the B1 language bill.

D66.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
D66.position: Governing party. The coalition agreement it signed with VVD and CDA commits to steering on 1.5% structural growth, working towards the 3% R&D norm, a national investment institution, an agency for disruptive innovation (NADI) and easier employee share options for start-ups. In the 3 September 2026 debate MP Oualhadj asked for AI test environments (sandboxes) before summer 2027 and for physical space where a company can build a first pilot plant without waiting years for permits; her motion to designate at least one innovation cluster as an accelerated permitting zone was adopted on 8 September 2026.

D66.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
D66.position: D66 is the largest coalition party. The coalition agreement it signed keeps the partial face-covering ban, aims to counter foreign funding of mosques and announces legislation for targeted supervision of weekend schools, while stating that racism and discrimination have no place. On 17 March 2026 D66 voted against the PVV motions on Islam and for the DENK motions against extra rules on amplified calls to prayer and for structural consultation with Muslim communities. In the Senate D66 voted against the foreign-funding transparency bill on 24 March 2026.

D66.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
D66.position: Coalition party. Calls the queue on the grid a national crisis and co-filed the adopted motion for the Crisis Act. Its manifesto pledges to reinforce the grid, invest in storage to reduce congestion, and keep modern gas plants open as long as needed for security of supply. Voted against the BBB motion on early capacity applications for housing.

D66.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
D66.position: The 2025 manifesto wants to shorten mandatory sick pay to one year and calls for fundamental reform of the WIA. In government D66 supplies the Minister of Social Affairs (Vijlbrief) and signed the coalition agreement that speaks of 'more workable' sick pay, abolishing the IVA for new cases and a lower maximum daily wage; the WIA measures were shelved in their proposed form in May 2026. D66 voted for the Ceulemans motion and for the Social Security Enforcement Act. In the report on bill 36 926 it warned the system could become even more complex.

D66.title: Tax burden on income and work
D66.position: Governing party (prime minister Rob Jetten). Its manifesto says allowances are too complex and that taxes hit workers harder than the wealthy, and proposes replacing allowances step by step with an individual basic amount. In November 2026 D66, with CDA, agreed the tax-shift amendment with PRO and Volt and voted for the amended 2027 Tax Plan.

VVD.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
VVD.position: The VVD supplies justice minister David van Weel, who coordinates the strategy. Its manifesto links rising hatred of Jews to poor integration and proposes an administrative ban on organisations such as Samidoun. In the debate MP Ellian called it unacceptable that Jewish institutions pay for their own security, criticised universities that end cooperation with Israeli universities and filed a motion to make the subsidy for Holocaust guest lessons structural.

VVD.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
VVD.position: Wants inflow of all forms of migration to fall and a new system in which all asylum applications are handled outside Europe and refugees come by invitation only, which it says could mean years without admitting asylum seekers. Until then it wants the strictest possible policy: closed reception and faster removal for nuisance-causing applicants, return hubs, and a legal ban on priority for status holders in social housing. The VVD voted against repealing the Spreidingswet on 23 June 2026 as a coalition party; its Senate group supported the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and the Pact implementation act.

VVD.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
VVD.position: Wants a capital gains tax, in which tax is paid only on realised returns, as fast as possible and opposes higher taxes on wealth. Voted for the February 2026 bill; VVD senators later threatened to vote against it, and VVD minister Heinen initiated the amending bill. Voted for the amending bill and for JA21's rejected amendment to cut the rate by 3 points, and against the 2027 Tax Plan after the two-rate amendment was adopted.

VVD.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
VVD.position: VVD wants 30 large new residential districts, fewer rules and shorter objection procedures, more affordable owner-occupied homes and a 'radical' loosening of rules on the rental market to attract investors. It wants to keep the mortgage interest deduction: its leader Yesilgöz said in September 2025 the party would not join a cabinet that changes it, and the coalition agreement keeps it unchanged.

VVD.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
VVD.position: The VVD wants moderate population growth in line with the State Commission, more selective labour migration, a 'top talent' scheme replacing the knowledge migrant scheme while keeping the 27% expat ruling, fewer international students outside shortage fields, and naturalisation after ten years with higher language, income or education requirements. In 2026 it voted for the labour-migration band, against the meat-sector agency ban, against work permits for EU workers and against 20-year naturalisation; its MP Michon-Derkzen submitted the adopted B1 motion.

VVD.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
VVD.position: Governing party. In the debate MP Martens-America said the Netherlands needs 1.5% to 2% growth, called for labour-market reform (she described the two-year sick-pay obligation as excessive and dismissal law as outdated), asked what the minister is doing to unlock private R&D spending, and said the cabinet response to Wennink came late and was brief. The VVD voted against the SP motion on a budget method that values the returns on investments and against replacing the second year of sick pay for small employers with a collective scheme. In November 2026 the VVD group in the House voted against the amended 2027 Tax Plan after an amendment by PRO and Volt shifted part of the tax burden from labour to wealth.

VVD.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
VVD.position: The VVD manifesto wants mosques and weekend schools to be transparent about funding, a cap of 50% on funding of religious organisations by foreign governments, quick handling of the informal-education supervision bill, a total ban on face-covering clothing and a municipal council veto on new schools. On 17 March 2026 the VVD voted against declaring that Islam does not belong to the Netherlands and against closing Islamic schools, and for the motions to ban the Muslim Brotherhood and to include political Islam and foreign mosque funding in the integration agenda. VVD senators voted for the transparency bill that the Senate rejected.

VVD.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
VVD.position: Coalition party. Its manifesto calls grid expansion a matter of national interest and wants to limit research burdens, legally protect electricity infrastructure and designate the Flevoland-Gelderland-Utrecht region as an innovation area. MP Müller said the Crisis Act has the very highest priority for the VVD and filed a motion asking that the House can speak out on time-of-use tariffs before ACM's final decision.

VVD.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
VVD.position: The manifesto proposes abolishing the second year of sick pay for small employers and replacing it with collective insurance, and reforming the Gatekeeper Improvement Act to cut bureaucracy. VVD supplies the Minister of Work and Participation (Aartsen), who sent the sick-pay scenarios. In the House, VVD called the pay obligation one of the heaviest burdens on employers, voted for the Ceulemans motion and for the Social Security Enforcement Act, and said it had supported SP's proposal on the second year.

VVD.title: Tax burden on income and work
VVD.position: Governing party. Its manifesto wants a simpler tax system in which work pays, an end to what it calls excessive levelling through allowances, deductions and credits, eventually no allowance system, and no tax increases on savings (box 3), enterprise (box 2) or inheritance and gifts. The VVD rejected the D66/CDA deal with PRO and Volt and voted against the 2027 Tax Plan on 12 November 2026 while remaining in the coalition.

PRO.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
PRO.position: PRO (the merged GroenLinks-PvdA; its MPs still spoke as GroenLinks-PvdA in April 2026) treats antisemitism alongside other forms of discrimination and stresses prevention and dialogue in schools, sport and online, together with criminal enforcement. MP Bromet said freedom to demonstrate leaves room to denounce the Netanyahu government provided Israel's right to exist within a two-state solution is not questioned and individual Jews are never held responsible. She co-signed three motions, with CDA, D66 and 50PLUS.

PRO.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
PRO.position: The merged GroenLinks-PvdA voted against repealing the Spreidingswet in the House (23 June 2026). In the Senate, where the group still sits as GroenLinks-PvdA, it requested roll-call votes and voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and against the Pact implementation act; Senator Karimi said the bills intrude deeply on asylum seekers' rights and that limiting family reunification is legally vulnerable. With the ChristenUnie, PRO obtained a House majority for a motion to examine state-owned property as long-term reception so that children do not end up in emergency shelter.

PRO.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
PRO.position: Voted for the February 2026 bill and against the amending bill, which it considers unnecessary, rushed and unfunded. Wants wealthy people rather than workers to pay for any shortfall. Together with Volt it proposed the amendment creating a 38.5% box 3 top rate, adopted on 12 November 2026 with D66 and CDA support.

PRO.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
PRO.position: PRO (the merged GroenLinks-PvdA; the sources cited still use the name GroenLinks-PvdA) wants to phase out the mortgage interest deduction in 8 to 12 years and use the proceeds to build affordable homes. Its motion to reverse the automatic increase in the deduction rate was adopted on 12 May 2026. In the Senate GroenLinks-PvdA voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

PRO.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
PRO.position: PRO (the merged GroenLinks-PvdA) focuses in parliament on abuses in labour migration: its MP Patijn submitted the adopted motion for an agency-work ban in the meat sector. It voted for the labour-migration band, for full implementation of the Roemer recommendations and for the SGP motion on non-EU labour migration as a last resort; against work permits for EU workers, against 20-year naturalisation and for the B1 bill. As GroenLinks-PvdA it voted against the motion to reconsider raising the knowledge-migrant salary criterion. Its 2025 manifesto could not be retrieved for this file.

PRO.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
PRO.position: Opposition. MP Van der Lee said 1.5% growth can be desirable but is not a goal in itself, asked why clean technology is not one of the cabinet's focus markets, and said about 15 billion euros of public money is needed to bring R&D to 3% of GDP. He said he would prefer a national investment bank and called a broad social accord including the trade unions crucial. His motion to let the investment institution act on non-market terms to fix market failures was rejected; his motion (co-signed by D66) to attach conditions to NADI so that value creation stays in the Netherlands and Europe was adopted. With Volt, PRO filed the amendment to the 2027 Tax Plan that shifted part of the tax burden from labour to wealth.

PRO.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
PRO.position: PRO (the merged GroenLinks-PvdA; listed under that name in the March 2026 voting record) voted on 17 March 2026 against all PVV motions on Islam and against the JA21 motion on political Islam, and for the DENK motions against extra rules on amplified calls to prayer and for structural consultation with Muslim communities. Its senators voted against the foreign-funding transparency bill on 24 March 2026. In March 2025 GL-PvdA supported DENK's request for a debate on the national study of discrimination against Muslims. Its MP Lahlah's motions in the March 2026 debate concerned civic integration funding, work routes and women status holders.

PRO.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
PRO.position: The parliamentary records cited list this group as GroenLinks-PvdA. MP Van Oosterhout filed motions to make energy saving an integral part of the congestion approach (adopted 2 June 2026), to study pilot installations with battery emergency power, and to evaluate the priority framework. The group voted for the Crisis Act motion and against permit-free expansion within existing transformer stations.

PRO.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
PRO.position: In the House (where the group was still recorded as GroenLinks-PvdA in spring 2026) the party opposed the lower maximum daily wage and filed motions, including one to reverse the abolition of the allowance for disabled people. On bill 36 926 it voiced concern about the position of employees and the dismissal ban during sickness. It voted against the Ceulemans motion on shortening sick pay and for the Social Security Enforcement Act.

PRO.title: Tax burden on income and work
PRO.position: The GL-PvdA manifesto (the merged party now sits as PRO) says tax on work goes down and taxes on income from wealth go up, wants to make allowances unnecessary step by step, and would phase out the expat ruling. PRO leader Jesse Klaver co-submitted the amendment that lowers the first-bracket rate and adds a box 3 top rate, and PRO voted for the amended Tax Plan.

PVV.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
PVV.position: The PVV attributes antisemitism to immigration and Islam and calls 'de-Islamisation' the solution. It wants Dutch nationality withdrawn from dual nationals convicted of antisemitic crimes, slogans such as 'from the river to the sea' made explicitly punishable and antisemitic demonstrations ended by police. Its manifesto ties support for Israel to rising antisemitism. In the debate MP Boon said the party condemns all forms of antisemitism, including from the right.

PVV.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
PVV.position: Wants an immediate asylum stop and repeal of the Spreidingswet, and tabled motions for both in the Senate (rejected 21 April 2026) and the House (rejected 23 June 2026, 45-100 on a roll call it requested). The amendment that criminalised illegal stay in the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet came from PVV MP Vondeling. Its Senate group called the Schoof-cabinet bills 'a step in the right direction', voted for them and for the Pact implementation act. In 2025 a PVV amendment banning any priority for status holders in social housing won a House majority.

PVV.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
PVV.position: Voted against both the February 2026 bill and the amending bill. NOS lists the PVV among parties favouring a full capital gains tax; MP Vlottes opposed taxing unrealised gains, criticised the speed of the process and called the funding phantom cover. The PVV asked in writing whether the cabinet should resign over the handling of the file.

PVV.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
PVV.position: The 2025 manifesto has a chapter 'Homes for the Dutch': a 10% cut in social rents with compensation for housing associations, keeping the mortgage interest deduction, a national crisis plan for housebuilding and no priority for status holders in social housing under any circumstances. A PVV amendment banning such priority was adopted by the House in July 2025 and later removed through the novelle; in the Senate the PVV voted against the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting and for the novelle.

PVV.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
PVV.position: The PVV manifesto calls for a stop to immigration from Islamic countries, a stop to family reunification, maximum restriction of study migration, an end to the expat ruling and naturalisation only after 15 years; it does not use the term labour migration. In parliament the PVV submitted motions for work permits for EU workers, an employer levy per labour migrant and 20-year naturalisation, all rejected. It voted against the CDA motion for a labour-migration band and against the FVD motion for a 60,000 cap, and for the meat-sector agency ban.

PVV.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
PVV.position: Opposition. MP Prickaertz said the PVV shares the analysis that the Netherlands must keep investing, innovating and growing, but objects to the government choosing strategic sectors; he argued small and medium-sized businesses need affordable energy, lower taxes and permits issued on time rather than a multi-billion fund for strategic technology. His motion against preferential treatment for specific sectors was rejected. The PVV was the only group to vote against the motion setting conditions for NADI, and also voted against the motions on a capital-market plan and on first choosing among existing economic plans.

PVV.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
PVV.position: The PVV manifesto states the party was founded to protect the Netherlands against 'islamisation'. It calls for a ban on Islamic education, a general burqa ban, a ban on the Islamic call to prayer, a ban on headscarves in government buildings and no immigration from Islamic countries; according to NOS, the 2023 calls to ban the Quran and mosques are not in the 2025 programme. In March 2026 PVV MPs Boon and Wilders tabled motions to declare that Islam does not belong to the Netherlands, to close all Islamic schools, to ban headscarves for underage girls at school and to ban the Muslim Brotherhood; only the last was adopted.

PVV.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
PVV.position: Wants to stop the energy transition and solve congestion by adding no wind turbines or solar parks, keeping coal and gas plants open and building nuclear plants. MP Kops filed motions to withdraw the offshore wind action plan, keep coal plants open, and prevent differentiated grid tariffs. The PVV voted for the Crisis Act motion on 2 June 2026.

PVV.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
PVV.position: PVV opposes the coalition's WIA cuts, in particular lowering benefits already being paid and abolishing the IVA. On bill 36 926 it asked why the government kept the 104-week obligation although earlier advice (the Borstlap committee) argued for shortening, and it voted for the Ceulemans motion and for the Social Security Enforcement Act. Its 2025 manifesto does not mention sick pay or the WIA; it does propose stopping the 'export of benefits and allowances'.

PVV.title: Tax burden on income and work
PVV.position: The PVV manifesto concentrates on VAT and excise rather than income tax rates: VAT on energy from 21% to 9%, no VAT on groceries, no fuel excise increase, 21% VAT on art and culture, and an end to the expat ruling. On 12 November 2026 PVV members Vlottes and Wilders tabled a motion of no confidence in the cabinet during the Tax Plan votes. The PVV is not among the groups reported as supporting the Tax Plan.

CDA.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
CDA.position: The coalition party CDA says there is no room for antisemitism and that it and Holocaust denial must be fought continuously. MP Tijs van den Brink framed the problem as one of society as a whole, including the Christian history of Jew-hatred in Europe, said the cabinet 'is not the problem today' and filed a motion on fighting online antisemitism among young people.

CDA.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
CDA.position: Coalition party that supplies the Minister of Asylum and Migration, Bart van den Brink. Supports the EU Pact and voted for its implementation act, and voted against repealing the Spreidingswet. In the Senate the CDA called the criminalisation of illegal stay 'a very nasty political quickie' and voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet once the novelle exempting helpers had been rejected, while asking for new proposals on declaring people undesirable, ending penalty payments and criminalising non-cooperation with return.

CDA.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
CDA.position: States it favours a full capital gains tax. Voted for the February 2026 bill; NOS reported that CDA senators later threatened to vote against it. Voted for the amending bill while questioning the funding and the process, and joined D66, PRO and Volt in the Tax Plan deal that raises tax on wealth. MP Inge van Dijk asked for a reform of the whole tax and benefits system rather than box 3 alone.

CDA.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
CDA.position: CDA's 2025 manifesto proposed phasing out the mortgage interest deduction over thirty years and using the money to lower income tax. In the coalition agreement it accepted leaving the deduction unchanged, and on 12 May 2026 it voted for the motion to reverse the automatic increase. In the Senate CDA voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

CDA.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
CDA.position: The CDA wants 'more grip on migration', a strong reduction in demand for labour migrants doing low-paid work, further implementation of the Roemer report, and employers who are responsible for housing and Dutch lessons. Its MP Tijs van den Brink submitted the adopted motion for a guiding band for labour migration. The CDA voted for the meat-sector agency ban, against work permits for EU workers, against 20-year naturalisation and for the B1 bill.

CDA.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
CDA.position: Governing party; the minister of Economic Affairs and Climate, Heleen Herbert, was described in the debate as a CDA minister. MP Bühler said a new economy cannot be built from The Hague alone and that regional ecosystems run into missing grid connections, permits blocked by nitrogen rules, lack of business space, talent shortages and insufficient growth capital. Her motion to make a 'breakthrough approach' for priority investment projects part of the Taskforce's assignment was adopted.

CDA.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
CDA.position: The CDA is a coalition party and signatory of the coalition agreement, which aims to counter foreign funding of mosques, keeps the partial face-covering ban and affirms freedom of education under Article 23. On 17 March 2026 the CDA voted against all PVV motions on Islam, including the Muslim Brotherhood ban, and for the JA21 motion to include political Islam, foreign mosque funding and salafist influence in the integration agenda. CDA senators voted against the transparency bill on 24 March 2026. In March 2025 the CDA opposed a debate on the national study of discrimination against Muslims, citing the small number of respondents.

CDA.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
CDA.position: Coalition party. Presented with D66 the December 2025 agenda that made congestion the highest priority. MP Jumelet filed the adopted motion for permit-free expansion within existing transformer stations and co-filed the adopted motion asking ACM to test investment plans for under-investment. Voted against the BBB motion on early capacity applications for housing.

CDA.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
CDA.position: Coalition party. CDA stresses prevention, faster assessments at UWV and agreement with unions and employers, and calls WIA inflow among young people with mental-health complaints worrying. It voted against the Ceulemans motion on scenarios to shorten sick pay and for the Social Security Enforcement Act. On bill 36 926 it asked how sick employees keep prospects of recovery and return.

CDA.title: Tax burden on income and work
CDA.position: Governing party. Its manifesto proposes phasing out mortgage interest relief step by step while lowering income tax by the same amount, a labour tax credit applied per hour worked, automatic payment of allowances, fewer income-dependent schemes to lower the marginal burden, and keeping the expat ruling. The coalition agreement left the mortgage interest deduction unchanged. CDA made the November 2026 deal with PRO and Volt together with D66 and voted for the Tax Plan.

JA21.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
JA21.position: JA21 sees 'increasing Islamisation' as an important, though not the only, factor in hatred of Jews. MP Nanninga called for less de-escalation and swifter punishment at universities, filed motions on sharing police data with universities so enrolments can be ended and on universities using the IHRA definition, and asked for the red triangle symbol to be covered by the glorification bill. The manifesto says universities should not give in to pressure to suspend ties with Israeli institutions.

JA21.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
JA21.position: Wants a sharp reduction of all immigration, a Danish-style model with reception in the region or partner countries, criminalisation of illegal stay and active removal. MP Ceulemans is first signatory of the initiative bill to repeal the Spreidingswet and said the party also wants to end asylum reception altogether. JA21 voted for all motions to repeal the law (23 June 2026); its Senate group supported the Schoof-cabinet bills and the Pact implementation act.

JA21.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
JA21.position: Wants tax only on what a person has actually earned, levied when the gain is realised. Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill. Wants crypto and precious metals included as soon as possible. Its amendment to lower the box 3 rate by 3 percentage points was rejected. NOS reported in September 2026 that JA21 made a budget deal conditional on a quick capital gains tax.

JA21.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
JA21.position: JA21 wants large-scale building inside and outside existing towns, faster procedures, exempting housebuilding from nitrogen restrictions, repeal of the Wet betaalbare huur and no automatic priority for status holders. NOS noted in 2025 that its manifesto did not mention the mortgage interest deduction. In the Senate JA21 voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

JA21.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
JA21.position: JA21 wants a sharp reduction of asylum, labour, family and study migration, no low-skilled labour migration from outside the EU, fewer foreign students and naturalisation after at least ten years. It voted for work permits for EU workers, for the labour-migration band, for the meat-sector agency ban and for the PVV's 20-year naturalisation motion; its MP Nanninga submitted the rejected motion for language level B2. It voted against cutting the expat ruling.

JA21.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
JA21.position: Opposition. MP Nanninga said the state has grown too large and businesses face too many rules, permits, subsidies and sustainability requirements, and that industry matters for national security. She said JA21 always opposed the National Growth Fund but has become less critical of an investment institution, on condition that economic return, productivity growth and Dutch strategic interest are central. Her motions for a capital-market improvement plan alongside the investment institution, and (with MP Keijzer) that policy on gender, origin or cultural background must not be an investment criterion, were both adopted.

JA21.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
JA21.position: JA21's manifesto has a section headed 'Islam en Westerse waarden', calls the growth of Islamic schools undesirable, wants a ban on foreign funding of mosques, strict supervision of informal Islamic education, a blacklist of preachers and no headscarves or other religious expressions for police, municipal enforcement officers (boa's) and other public officials. On 17 March 2026 JA21 voted against the PVV motions to declare that Islam does not belong to the Netherlands and to close Islamic schools, and for the headscarf ban for underage girls at school and the Muslim Brotherhood ban. Its own motion to include political Islam, foreign mosque funding and salafist influence in the integration agenda was adopted. JA21 senators voted for the transparency bill.

JA21.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
JA21.position: Wants to solve congestion with a focus on nuclear power and by not writing off fossil fuels. MP Van den Berg filed motions for gas-hybrid heat pumps in new homes, a capacity mechanism, a fast-track route for transformer and high-voltage stations (adopted) and continuous updating of demand forecasts (adopted unanimously). Co-filed a motion on energy tax for household storage.

JA21.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
JA21.position: JA21 wants mandatory sick pay cut, preferably to one year for all employers, and regards bill 36 926 as an intermediate step. Its MP Ceulemans filed the motion, adopted on 31 March 2026, asking for scenarios to shorten sick pay. The manifesto asks for shorter sick pay, faster reintegration and reform of the system. JA21 voted against the Social Security Enforcement Act.

JA21.title: Tax burden on income and work
JA21.position: JA21's manifesto proposes a new, strongly simplified tax system to lower the marginal burden, abolishing allowances and tax credits in favour of a simple system of 'toelagen', and abolishing box 2 by taxing substantial shareholdings in box 3. According to Taxlive, JA21 worked together with SGP and BBB during the Tax Plan debate and set far-reaching conditions for support; IamExpat reports the three threatened to vote against the box 3 reform if the wealth-tax changes were adopted.

Groep Markuszower.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
Groep Markuszower.position: The group, which split from the PVV in January 2026 and has no election manifesto of its own, says the Netherlands 'imports' antisemitism and that it grows through a lack of backbone among administrators. It wants campus bans and loss of study visas for students who glorify terrorism or occupy buildings, dismissal of university administrators who do not protect Jews, and antisemitic demonstrations banned immediately.

Groep Markuszower.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
Groep Markuszower.position: The group that split from the PVV in January 2026 voted for all motions to repeal the Spreidingswet and to end compulsion on municipalities (23 June 2026). MP Markuszower, after whom the group is named, argues that an asylum stop alone is not enough and asked the minister for a plan with a timetable for large-scale return of people without lawful residence and for systematic withdrawal of permits obtained with invented stories.

Groep Markuszower.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
Groep Markuszower.position: Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill. It was one of two groups, with FVD, that voted for abolishing box 3 through a 0% rate, and it supported the rejected amendment to lower the rate by 3 percentage points.

Groep Markuszower.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
Groep Markuszower.position: No housing programme, position page or housing statement of this House group was found in the sources consulted for this file.

Groep Markuszower.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
Groep Markuszower.position: The group, formed by MPs who left the PVV group in January 2026, has no election manifesto of its own. In 2026 it voted for work permits for EU workers, for an employer levy per labour migrant, for 20-year naturalisation and for language levels B1 and B2, and also for the CDA motion for a labour-migration band. It voted against the agency-work ban in the meat sector.

Groep Markuszower.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
Groep Markuszower.position: Opposition. The group did not speak in the 3 September 2026 debate on the Wennink report. In the votes of 8 September 2026 it supported, among others, the motions on a budget method that values the returns on investments, on conditions for NADI, on a capital-market plan, on an accelerated permitting zone for an innovation cluster, and the PVV motion against preferential treatment for specific sectors.

Groep Markuszower.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
Groep Markuszower.position: Groep Markuszower, which split from the PVV in January 2026, voted on 17 March 2026 for all PVV motions on Islam: declaring that Islam does not belong to the Netherlands, closing all Islamic schools, a headscarf ban for underage girls at school and a ban on the Muslim Brotherhood. It was the only group besides the PVV to vote for closing all Islamic schools. Its MP Lammers criticised the PVV for not saying how the closure should be arranged.

Groep Markuszower.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
Groep Markuszower.position: MP Moinat filed a motion stating that the grid is stalling due to a shortage of controllable power and asking to invest only in energy sources not dependent on wind or sun; it was rejected on 2 June 2026. The group voted for the Crisis Act motion.

Groep Markuszower.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
Groep Markuszower.position: The group voted for the Ceulemans motion on scenarios to shorten sick pay and against the Social Security Enforcement Act. In the March 2026 budget debate its MP Moinat criticised UWV's errors in WIA benefits and said the system too often distrusts and sanctions instead of guiding people.

Groep Markuszower.title: Tax burden on income and work
Groep Markuszower.position: The group has no 2025 manifesto of its own (it split from the PVV in January 2026). On the 2027 Tax Plan, Markuszower submitted amendments to apply the full inflation correction in 2027 and to raise the labour tax credit, and a motion to abolish the freedom contribution for businesses as well.

FVD.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
FVD.position: The FVD manifesto does not mention antisemitism. On the Middle East it calls for a two-state solution, recognition of a Palestinian state within the 1967 borders and the release of Israeli hostages. FVD did not take part in the April 2026 debate on the taskforce report. Prime minister Jetten said in March 2026 that he was referring to FVD when he spoke of a party where someone who has been openly antisemitic can stand in municipal elections, and asked party leader De Vos to distance herself from antisemitism in her party; D66 repeated that call in the debate.

FVD.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
FVD.position: Wants to stop asylum reception in the Netherlands, dismantle COA, accept applications only at consulates in conflict regions, criminalise illegal stay and leave treaties such as Schengen and the UN Refugee Convention. FVD co-signed the initiative bill to repeal the Spreidingswet. In the Senate it voted for all three Schoof-cabinet bills, calling the novelle 'bad' but honouring an agreement, and voted against the Pact implementation act because it wants the Netherlands itself to decide who enters.

FVD.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
FVD.position: Opposes taxing savings and investments as such and wants box 3 abolished. Voted against both the February 2026 bill and the amending bill. Its amendment to set the rate at 0% was rejected; it also proposed keeping the shareholder borrowing cap at EUR 500,000, which was rejected.

FVD.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
FVD.position: FVD wants 100,000 homes a year, the scrapping of climate and nitrogen rules for building, repeal of the Wet betaalbare huur, a limited social-rent sector with priority for Dutch citizens over status holders, and a mortgage interest deduction at a higher rate. In the Senate FVD voted against both the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting and the novelle.

FVD.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
FVD.position: FVD wants a ten-year stop on naturalisation, abolition of the permanent residence permit, and a strictly regulated 'GreenCard' model of temporary work permits without prospect of naturalisation. It submitted the rejected motions for a net migration cap of 60,000 and for phasing out or further cutting the expat ruling. It voted against the CDA band motion, against the Roemer motion and against the meat-sector agency ban, and for 20-year naturalisation.

FVD.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
FVD.position: Opposition. MP Schenk said the Wennink report describes symptoms of political choices (regulatory burden he attributes to transfers of power to Brussels, neglected education, energy prices he attributes to the energy transition) and that its remedies amount to a merger of big government and big business; he said less government is needed, not more. FVD co-filed motions to give food and agriculture a full position in the follow-up and to make the prosperity of the Dutch population leading in the 1.5% growth aim; both were rejected.

FVD.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
FVD.position: The FVD 2025 manifesto focuses on stopping immigration and encouraging remigration and does not contain the word 'islam'. On 17 March 2026 FVD voted for the PVV motions to declare that Islam does not belong to the Netherlands and to ban the Muslim Brotherhood, and against closing all Islamic schools and against the headscarf ban for underage girls at school. FVD senators voted against the foreign-funding transparency bill on 24 March 2026.

FVD.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
FVD.position: Wants to stop the energy transition entirely, withdraw the Climate Act, nationalise the energy sector to prevent blackouts and build ten nuclear plants. Voted against the Crisis Act motion and against the motion asking ACM to test investment plans on 2 June 2026.

FVD.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
FVD.position: The manifesto limits sick pay to one year and relaxes dismissal law for small and medium-sized firms. FVD voted for the Ceulemans motion and against the Social Security Enforcement Act.

FVD.title: Tax burden on income and work
FVD.position: FVD's manifesto proposes a 20% flat tax on box 1 income, a tax-free threshold of EUR 30,000 for workers and pensioners, VAT rates of 6% and 19%, no VAT on business-to-business transactions and a phased abolition of the 30% ruling so that expats pay as much tax as Dutch people.

ChristenUnie.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
ChristenUnie.position: The ChristenUnie calls security of Jewish institutions a public responsibility that should not depend on fundraising within a minority community. MP Bikker co-initiated the law making a discriminatory motive a ground for a higher sentence. The manifesto wants the action plan against antisemitism continued and extended where needed and a taskforce in education so that fewer Jewish young people decide to study abroad.

ChristenUnie.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
ChristenUnie.position: Wants fast and fair procedures, stable small-scale reception and fair distribution; the Spreidingswet should stay. It commits to the EU Pact with human-rights safeguards but its Senate group voted against the Dutch implementation act because of the added national measures, and against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet. It opposes criminalising illegal stay and wants rooted children to receive a right of residence, while favouring registration of asylum applications outside Europe.

ChristenUnie.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
ChristenUnie.position: Voted against both the February 2026 bill and the amending bill. Asked the cabinet to follow the Council of State and move in one step in 2030, and said the minister missed a chance for better funding through gift tax. Its amendment allowing a cost deduction for real estate under the rebuttal scheme was adopted. Supported the 2027 Tax Plan including the two box 3 rates.

ChristenUnie.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
ChristenUnie.position: ChristenUnie wants 100,000 new homes a year, at least two-thirds affordable including 30% social rent, a levy on land-value gains ('planbatenheffing') and 20 billion euros extra over the coming decade. It supports phasing out the mortgage interest deduction over at least fifteen years. In the Senate it voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

ChristenUnie.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
ChristenUnie.position: The ChristenUnie manifesto chooses moderate growth on the basis of the State Commission's advice and a reduction in the number of study migrants. It was one of three parties voting for the 60,000 cap, co-submitted the motion for work permits for workers from Central and Eastern Europe, and voted for the labour-migration band, the Roemer motion and the meat-sector agency ban. It voted against 20-year naturalisation and for the B1 bill.

ChristenUnie.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
ChristenUnie.position: Opposition. MP Grinwis said grid tariffs for industry are much too high compared with neighbouring countries and that policy unpredictability destroys willingness to invest. He suggested the state take stakes in strategic sectors and conclude contracts that cover companies against policy risk, and said he misses 'Rhineland' stakeholder thinking in the Wennink report. His motion with the SGP to explore protecting companies against policy risks during the payback period of large investments was adopted.

ChristenUnie.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
ChristenUnie.position: The ChristenUnie manifesto, referring to the POCOB inquiry, wants to restrict money flows from unfree countries to mosques and informal Islamic education and to strive for banning organisations that exert such influence. On 17 March 2026 the party voted against the PVV motions to declare that Islam does not belong to the Netherlands, to close Islamic schools and to ban headscarves for girls, and for the Muslim Brotherhood ban and the JA21 motion on political Islam. ChristenUnie senators voted against the transparency bill on 24 March 2026.

ChristenUnie.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
ChristenUnie.position: The manifesto has a section 'Reduce grid congestion' and proposes a capital injection of €10 billion for grid operators, lower grid tariffs for projects that relieve the grid, and rules for home batteries including a mandatory option for the operator to switch them on and off. MP Grinwis filed adopted motions to evaluate the FGU crisis and to have ACM test investment plans.

ChristenUnie.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
ChristenUnie.position: The manifesto calls the disability insurance system needlessly complicated, wants to harmonise the WIA schemes, add a tailored scheme for terminally ill people and find a solution for people who are less than 35% disabled. In the House it asked the government for an international comparison of sick-pay rules and whether the duration could differ by employer size. It voted for the Ceulemans motion and the Social Security Enforcement Act.

ChristenUnie.title: Tax burden on income and work
ChristenUnie.position: The manifesto proposes replacing the allowance system with a simple basic credit that does not depend on income and a payable tax credit, and criticises the size of the labour tax credit. ChristenUnie MP Grinwis was first signatory of two amendments adopted on 12 November 2026 that lower the first two box 1 rates and keep the elderly tax credit intact, and the party voted for the amended Tax Plan.

SP.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
SP.position: The SP manifesto addresses the subject in its passage on Israel and Palestine: it calls equating justified criticism of Israel's policy with antisemitism unacceptable and says such criticism must not be criminalised. The SP had no speaker in the April 2026 debate on the taskforce report.

SP.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
SP.position: Says people fleeing war and violence should be received humanely while those with no claim must return as quickly as possible, and wants a net migration ceiling of 40,000 achieved mainly by cutting labour, knowledge and study migration. It wants refugees housed more often in rich municipalities. The SP voted against repealing the Spreidingswet; its Senate group voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and the Pact implementation act, calling the refusal of transitional rules inhumane.

SP.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
SP.position: Voted for the February 2026 bill and against the amending bill. In the Senate the SP voted against the motion stating no objection to withdrawing the original bill. The SP is not among the groups that filed written questions on the amending bill.

SP.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
SP.position: SP wants rents to go down, more social rental homes, a separate ministry and a national building plan. It wants to guarantee the mortgage interest deduction for homes up to 600,000 euros and phase it out faster above that. SP MP Beckerman questioned the minister in April 2026 about investors selling rental homes. In the Senate SP voted against the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

SP.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
SP.position: The SP wants work permits for workers from Central and Eastern Europe and full implementation of the Roemer recommendations; its motion on Roemer was adopted in June 2026 (136 in favour), its work-permit motion and a motion to extend Dutch-language requirements to everyone who comes to work or study for more than three months were rejected. It voted for the 60,000 cap, the employer levy, the meat-sector agency ban and cutting the expat ruling, and against 20-year naturalisation. Its 2025 manifesto could not be retrieved for this file.

SP.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
SP.position: Opposition. MP Jimmy Dijk called the Wennink report one-sided, describing it as a plan of CEOs, VNO-NCW and consultants that leads to more public spending, debt and risk for ordinary people and private profits for shareholders. He said the SP wants a different economic model that puts people before profit. His motion for a budget method that correctly values the benefits of investments was adopted; his motion with MP Keijzer to replace the second year of sick pay for small employers with a collective scheme was also adopted. The SP voted against the motion for a capital-market plan.

SP.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
SP.position: The SP manifesto does not mention Islam, mosques or Muslims; it addresses segregation in schools and neighbourhoods and discrimination in general terms. On 17 March 2026 the SP voted against all PVV motions on Islam and against the JA21 motion on political Islam, for DENK's motion on structural consultation with Muslim communities, and against DENK's motion to refrain from extra rules on amplified calls to prayer. SP senators voted against the transparency bill. In March 2025 the SP supported DENK's request for a debate on the national study of discrimination against Muslims.

SP.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
SP.position: Voted for the Crisis Act motion and the other adopted congestion motions on 2 June 2026. MP Jimmy Dijk filed a motion on 3 June 2026 to lower VAT on energy to the low rate. According to Solar & Storage Magazine the SP manifesto calls for 'sun on every roof'.

SP.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
SP.position: SP opposes the WIA and unemployment-benefit cuts and proposed collective financing of the second sick year for small and medium-sized firms with up to 50 employees. It wants less spending on low-value enforcement and recovery while keeping targeted fraud investigations. An SP motion adopted earlier states that money in the disability fund may only be used to improve disability schemes. SP voted against the Ceulemans motion and for the Social Security Enforcement Act.

SP.title: Tax burden on income and work
SP.position: The SP manifesto says it will lower income tax substantially and cut VAT on basic products, raise tax on income from capital to the level of income tax, and introduce a 5% millionaires' tax on wealth above EUR 5 million. SP MPs submitted amendments to reverse the narrowing of the healthcare cost deduction and to raise the high corporate tax rate; an SP motion against funding defence through the disability fund contribution was supported by all opposition parties. The SP is not among the groups reported as supporting the Tax Plan.

PvdD.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
PvdD.position: The PvdD says hatred of Jews must be tackled hard and that antisemitism occurs in all layers of society, and objects to what it calls its instrumental use against Muslims. It defends the right to demonstrate, wants the bill on glorification of terrorism withdrawn and filed a motion for a working definition that separates antisemitism from criticism of the Israeli government. MP Teunissen also asked about right-wing extremist conspiracy theories.

PvdD.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
PvdD.position: Voted against repealing the Spreidingswet in the House. In the Senate the Volt senator spoke partly on behalf of the PvdD against the Schoof-cabinet bills, and PvdD senators voted against the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and the Pact implementation act; Senator Koffeman said the implementation act carries the spirit of former minister Faber.

PvdD.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
PvdD.position: Voted for the February 2026 bill and against the amending bill. Supported the 2027 Tax Plan, including the two box 3 rates; NOS reports the party was persuaded shortly before the vote in exchange for commitments on other subjects.

PvdD.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
PvdD.position: According to NOS, the PvdD's 2025 manifesto wants to end the mortgage interest deduction for homes above the NHG purchase limit. In the Senate the PvdD voted against the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting and the novelle. The party's own housing page could not be opened for this file.

PvdD.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
PvdD.position: The PvdD voted for the Roemer motion and the meat-sector agency ban, and for phasing out the expat ruling. It voted against the labour-migration band, against the SGP motions on the State Commission and non-EU labour migration, against 20-year naturalisation and against the B1 bill. It supported the 2025 motion for work permits for Central and Eastern European workers but voted against the PVV's EU work-permit motion in March 2026. Its manifesto could not be retrieved for this file.

PvdD.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
PvdD.position: Opposition. The PvdD did not speak in the 3 September 2026 debate on the Wennink report. In the votes of 8 September 2026 it supported the motions on a budget method that values the returns on investments, on replacing the second year of sick pay for small employers with a collective scheme, on conditions for NADI and on studying how investments can be placed outside the regular expenditure frameworks; it voted against the motions on a capital-market plan, on the breakthrough approach for investment projects, on a launching-customer role for European AI companies and on protecting companies against policy risk.

PvdD.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
PvdD.position: On 17 March 2026 the PvdD voted against all PVV motions on Islam and against the JA21 motion on political Islam, and for all four DENK motions, including those against extra rules on amplified calls to prayer and for structural consultation with Muslim communities. PvdD senators voted against the transparency bill on 24 March 2026. In March 2025 the PvdD supported DENK's request for a debate on the national study of discrimination against Muslims.

PvdD.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
PvdD.position: Voted against the Crisis Act motion, against the fast-track route for transformer and high-voltage stations and against permit-free expansion within existing stations on 2 June 2026; voted for the motions on energy saving and early capacity applications for housing. Rejects nuclear power according to Solar & Storage Magazine.

PvdD.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
PvdD.position: PvdD voted against the Ceulemans motion on scenarios to shorten sick pay and for the Social Security Enforcement Act. No statements by the party on sick pay or the WIA were found in the debates and documents consulted for this file.

PvdD.title: Tax burden on income and work
PvdD.position: The manifesto says income tax will be made fairer with a lower low rate, wants 0% VAT on vegetables, fruit, grains, pulses and nuts, lower VAT on repairs and an end to the reduced VAT rate on ornamental plants. PvdD MP Teunissen submitted a series of amendments; the one adding EUR 100 to the flight tax for private jets from 2030 was adopted. IamExpat, citing NOS, reports the party first opposed the Tax Plan but voted for it after commitments on private jets and train fares.

SGP.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
SGP.position: The SGP devotes a chapter of its manifesto to standing 'beside the Jewish people, against antisemitism'. It wants antisemitic slogans, flags and images at demonstrations banned with the IHRA definition leading. In the debate MP Diederik van Dijk linked antisemitism to what he called excessive attention for the state of Israel and filed a motion for a public campaign.

SGP.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
SGP.position: Voted for repealing the Spreidingswet in the House (23 June 2026). In the Senate the SGP saw the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet as a means to gain control but voted against it once the novelle protecting people who help undocumented migrants was rejected; it voted for the Pact implementation act. It asks for better IND assessment of persecuted Christians.

SGP.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
SGP.position: Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill, which it calls a step in the right direction, and wants all assets under a capital gains tax as soon as possible. Its senator Schalk tabled the rejected Senate motion on withdrawing the original bill. Its amendment to defer tax on leased farmland passed on by inheritance or gift was rejected; its motion asking for a further inventory of improvements was adopted. NOS reported that SGP and JA21 called lowering the tax-free thresholds unacceptable.

SGP.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
SGP.position: According to NOS, the SGP does not want to abolish the mortgage interest deduction but 'is not opposed to a revision'. In the Senate the SGP voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting. No further SGP housing text was verified for this file.

SGP.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
SGP.position: The SGP manifesto says the number of labour migrants must come down and wants naturalisation after ten years with language level B1. Its MP Flach submitted the adopted motions to give high priority to the State Commission's report and to consider non-EU labour migration only as a last resort. The SGP voted for work permits for EU workers and the employer levy, against the meat-sector agency ban, against the SP's Roemer motion and against 20-year naturalisation.

SGP.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
SGP.position: Opposition. MP Flach said the SGP wants a national business accord with long-term agreements on investment, taxes and the business climate, and a cabinet-wide reduction target for regulatory burden measured in time and cost to businesses rather than number of rules. He called Wennink's reasoning on nitrogen and agriculture elitist and short-sighted. The SGP co-filed the adopted motion on protecting companies against policy risk.

SGP.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
SGP.position: The SGP manifesto has a passage headed 'Tegen islamisering' ('Against islamisation') that criticises the growth of amplified calls to prayer and of iftar meals at government bodies, and says Islamic calls to prayer with sound amplification do not belong in public space. It opposes general supervision of informal education such as in churches. On 17 March 2026 the SGP voted for declaring that Islam does not belong to the Netherlands and for the Muslim Brotherhood ban, and against closing all Islamic schools and the school headscarf ban. SGP senators voted for the transparency bill.

SGP.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
SGP.position: The manifesto says tackling congestion, smarter use of capacity and fast grid reinforcement deserve the highest priority, and calls for faster procedures and a nitrogen exemption for transformers and cables. MP Flach filed the adopted motion on legal obstacles to temporary flexibility solutions and a motion on VAT on rising grid tariffs.

SGP.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
SGP.position: The manifesto shortens mandatory sick pay from two to one and a half years as a first step, wants UWV put in order and lets private providers take over work such as clearing the UWV queue. SGP called bill 36 926 a very limited relief for employers, listed shortening sick pay among its wishes in the June 2026 debate, and voted for the Ceulemans motion and the Social Security Enforcement Act.

SGP.title: Tax burden on income and work
SGP.position: The SGP manifesto states that the burden on labour is lowered and that the allowance system must be overhauled. SGP MP Stoffer submitted amendments on the youngtimer company-car rule (adopted) and on keeping the small brewers' excise discount. Taxlive reports SGP acted together with JA21 and BBB during the Tax Plan debate.

BBB.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
BBB.position: BBB says the Jewish community must be protected unconditionally. Its manifesto wants educational institutions to act immediately against antisemitic or other hateful demonstrations and the Education Inspectorate to take this into account. In the debate Van der Plas said university policy against antisemitism does not work and argued that parliamentary motions on boycotting Israeli products make Jews in the Netherlands feel unsafe.

BBB.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
BBB.position: Co-initiator of the bill to repeal the Spreidingswet and voted for all repeal motions. Its Senate group voted for the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet and the Pact implementation act, saying temporary protection must actually be temporary. MP Vermeer asked that crime and nuisance figures be published per reception location.

BBB.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
BBB.position: Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill, which it says brings taxation closer to gains actually realised. MP Vermeer objected that the amending bill departs from the usual budget rules. In the Senate, BBB senator Kroon criticised the handling of a bill the cabinet itself intended to change and tabled a motion on a capital gains-based law.

BBB.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
BBB.position: BBB's 2025 manifesto says the mortgage interest deduction should not be limited further, according to NOS. BBB supplied the housing minister, Keijzer, in the previous cabinet; she introduced the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting and the bill to end priority for status holders, and proposed loosening the Wet betaalbare huur. In the Senate BBB voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

BBB.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
BBB.position: BBB's motion asking the cabinet to weigh the economic and social dependence on labour migration in all sectors was adopted in June 2026 (90 in favour). BBB voted against the labour-migration band, against work permits for EU workers, against the meat-sector agency ban and against the Roemer motion, and for 20-year naturalisation and language levels B1 and B2. Its manifesto could not be retrieved for this file.

BBB.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
BBB.position: Opposition. MP Vermeer named the nitrogen law, grid congestion and constantly changing policy as the main causes of a worsening business climate, and asked why agrifood is not one of the cabinet's six strategic markets and why roads, bridges and waterways are not treated as economic infrastructure. His motion with the SP to include physical mobility infrastructure was adopted; his motion with FVD on food and agriculture was rejected. He also put written questions to ministers about the national investment institution on 2 September 2026.

BBB.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
BBB.position: On 17 March 2026 BBB voted for the PVV motions to declare that Islam does not belong to the Netherlands, to ban headscarves for underage girls at school and to ban the Muslim Brotherhood, and against closing all Islamic schools. It voted for the JA21 motion on political Islam. BBB senators voted against the foreign-funding transparency bill on 24 March 2026. In March 2025 BBB opposed a debate on the national study of discrimination against Muslims; NOS reported the party found the study 'rattles on all sides'.

BBB.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
BBB.position: MP Vermeer filed the adopted motion on early capacity applications for housing projects and a motion for a structural financing scheme for grid-aware new construction, and asked the cabinet to make better use of gas-fired combined heat and power. In October 2026 he pressed for a solution to double energy tax on home batteries and electric cars before 1 January 2027.

BBB.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
BBB.position: BBB voted for the Ceulemans motion on scenarios to shorten sick pay and against the Social Security Enforcement Act. In the June 2026 debate its MP Vermeer criticised lowering benefits as a response to UWV waiting times and the use of the disability-fund premium for other purposes.

BBB.title: Tax burden on income and work
BBB.position: BBB's manifesto calls the tax and allowance system needlessly complex, wants fixed amounts as an allowance instead of complex schemes, a simpler tax on labour, and no increase in taxes on savings (box 3) or enterprise (box 2). BBB MP Vermeer submitted an amendment for further cuts in fuel excise and a motion to scrap the VAT increase on ornamental horticulture for good.

DENK.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
DENK.position: DENK says there is no room for hatred of Jewish Dutch people and expresses solidarity after the March 2026 attacks, while warning that the fight against antisemitism is misused to stifle political criticism of Israel and that the IHRA definition lets anti-Zionism and antisemitism run together. Its manifesto lists antisemitism among forms of discrimination it fights and calls for a specific plan; the same manifesto wants the Netherlands to recognise Zionism as an extremist and racist ideology.

DENK.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
DENK.position: Voted against all motions to repeal the Spreidingswet or to end the duty on municipalities, and for the motions on spreading good practices and on using state property for long-term reception (23 June 2026).

DENK.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
DENK.position: Voted against both the February 2026 bill and the amending bill, and for the adopted cost deduction amendment. Supported the 2027 Tax Plan including the two box 3 rates. MP Ergin called it unacceptable that the minister worked with Groep Markuszower to win support.

DENK.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
DENK.position: According to NOS, DENK's 2025 manifesto wants to end the mortgage interest deduction 'for rich property owners', meaning homes above 500,000 euros. No further DENK housing text was verified for this file.

DENK.title: Immigration: labour, study, family migration and naturalisation
DENK.position: DENK voted for the Roemer motion and for phasing out the expat ruling. It voted against the labour-migration band, against the SGP motions on the State Commission and non-EU labour migration, against work permits for EU workers, against the meat-sector agency ban, and against 20-year naturalisation and the B1 and B2 language motions. Its manifesto could not be retrieved for this file.

DENK.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
DENK.position: Opposition. DENK did not speak in the 3 September 2026 debate on the Wennink report. In the votes of 8 September 2026 it supported, among others, the motions on a budget method that values the returns on investments, on letting the investment institution act on non-market terms, on conditions for NADI and on studying investments outside the regular expenditure frameworks; MP Van Baarle stated afterwards that DENK wished to be recorded as in favour of the motion on an accelerated permitting zone.

DENK.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
DENK.position: DENK's manifesto has a section 'Bestrijding moslimhaat' (combating hatred of Muslims): a National Coordinator against Muslim hatred, government funding for security of mosques, a legal ban on burning the Quran and other holy books, explicit protection of the Islamic call to prayer, and repeal of the niqab ban and of the bills on informal education and civil-society transparency, which it calls 'Islamophobic bullying laws'. In March 2026 DENK MP Ergin tabled motions to abolish the term 'integration', to recognise the 'integration paradox', to refrain from extra rules on amplified calls to prayer and for structural consultation with Muslim communities; all four were rejected.

DENK.title: Grid congestion: the full electricity network
DENK.position: Voted for the Crisis Act motion and the other adopted congestion motions on 2 June 2026. MP El Abassi filed motions in June 2026 on energy poverty and lowering energy tax, not on the grid itself.

DENK.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
DENK.position: DENK opposes the planned cuts for disabled people and said the plans to trim the WIA and unemployment benefit must be withdrawn. It voted against the Ceulemans motion on shortening sick pay and for the Social Security Enforcement Act.

DENK.title: Tax burden on income and work
DENK.position: DENK's manifesto wants the allowance system replaced, no VAT on fruit and vegetables, lower VAT generally, and a fairer distribution within income tax by asking more of the very rich. DENK MP Ergin filed motions to lower taxes on fuel and on groceries. DENK voted for the amended Tax Plan.

50PLUS.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
50PLUS.position: 50PLUS focused in the debate on Holocaust education, which MP Struijs said falls short, and on Jewish police officers who say they feel unsafe within the force. It filed a motion for independent research into how the Holocaust is taught.

50PLUS.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
50PLUS.position: Voted against repealing the Spreidingswet but for a motion asking the government to formulate concrete conditions for repeal. Its senator voted for the Asielnoodmaatregelenwet, criticising D66 for not doing so, and for the Pact implementation act.

50PLUS.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
50PLUS.position: Voted against the February 2026 bill and for the amending bill. MP Van Brenk said signals from implementing bodies must be heeded and the amending bill should take effect later if they have too little time; the group asked how capital flight is monitored. Supported the 2027 Tax Plan according to the reported vote.

50PLUS.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
50PLUS.position: Opposition. MP Van Brenk said the Wennink and Draghi reports are a wake-up call, noted that earlier strategic choices for green technology did not make the Netherlands or Europe a leader in solar panels, wind turbines or batteries, and asked why regulatory burden is outside the Taskforce's scope. Her motion to turn regulatory-burden reduction into a taskforce with measurable goals was rejected.

50PLUS.title: Islam, integration and the 'islamisation' debate
50PLUS.position: On 17 March 2026 50PLUS voted against the PVV motions to declare that Islam does not belong to the Netherlands, to close Islamic schools and to ban headscarves for girls at school, and for the Muslim Brotherhood ban and the JA21 motion on political Islam. 50PLUS senators voted against the transparency bill on 24 March 2026.

50PLUS.title: Sick leave, disability benefits and fraud
50PLUS.position: 50PLUS opposes abolishing the IVA and lowering the maximum daily wage and criticised repeated reassessments of older workers by UWV. It voted against the Ceulemans motion and for the Social Security Enforcement Act.

50PLUS.title: Tax burden on income and work
50PLUS.position: The 50PLUS manifesto calls for full application of the statutory inflation correction in income tax. MP Van Brenk co-signed the adopted Grinwis/Van Brenk amendment lowering tax on work, and leader Jan Struijs questioned in the debate whether people with only a state pension benefit from the first-bracket cut. 50PLUS voted for the amended Tax Plan.

Lid Keijzer.title: Antisemitism: incidents, security and the policy response
Lid Keijzer.position: Mona Keijzer argues that the anti-Western far left and Islamic extremism have formed an alliance, that slogans presented as anti-Zionism have an antisemitic core, and that a considerable part of antisemitism is imported, including by international students. She asked whether student visas can be revoked and why demonstrations inside universities are not prohibited. According to the minister, a motion of hers asking the government to bring the glorification-of-terrorism bill was adopted on 21 April 2026.

Lid Keijzer.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
Lid Keijzer.position: Voted for the amending bill and for the rejected amendment to lower the box 3 rate by 3 percentage points. Said in the plenary debate that the current box 3 tax drives entrepreneurs out of the country and argued for a tax that those who pay it experience as fair.

Lid Keijzer.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
Lid Keijzer.position: Opposition. MP Keijzer opposed Wennink's proposals for a commissioner for future prosperity and a taskforce, and called for shorter permit deadlines, removal of Dutch additions to EU rules, a solution to the nitrogen deadlock without sacrificing agriculture, long-term tax certainty and changes to box 3 (the tax on savings and investments). Her motion on short-term box 3 relief was rejected.

Volt.title: Asylum: applications, reception, returns and fraud
Volt.position: Wants a humane, common European refugee policy with redistribution between member states, and an end to internal border checks. Voted against repealing the Spreidingswet; in the Senate it requested roll-call votes and voted against all three Schoof-cabinet bills and against the Pact implementation act.

Volt.title: Box 3: tax on savings and investments
Volt.position: Voted for the February 2026 bill and against the amending bill. MP Dassen described the amending bill as a gift to people in box 2 at the expense of future generations. Co-proposer with PRO of the adopted Tax Plan amendment creating two box 3 rates.

Volt.title: Housing: cost and shortage of homes
Volt.position: According to NOS, Volt wants to phase out the mortgage interest deduction 'as soon as possible'. In the Senate Volt voted for the Wet versterking regie volkshuisvesting.

Volt.title: Innovation, productivity and the business climate
Volt.position: Opposition. MP Dassen said the finance minister's approach to the budget blocks long-term investment, asked when the investment bank will be ready, and said much computing power on European soil is owned or bought up by American companies. His motion to use the government's launching-customer role for European AI companies was adopted, as was his motion with PRO to first choose which existing economic plans will be carried out; his motion to study placing investments outside the regular expenditure frameworks was rejected. With PRO, Volt filed the amendment to the 2027 Tax Plan that shifted part of the tax burden from labour to wealth.

Volt.title: Tax burden on income and work
Volt.position: Volt's manifesto proposes more box 1 brackets combined with a basic income, and aligning expat rulings between EU member states. Volt's Dassen co-submitted the adopted tax-shift amendment with PRO's Klaver, and Volt voted for the amended Tax Plan.
